annotation.cut_point:
We are given the following system of congruences:

$$
\begin{align*}
x &\equiv 1 \pmod{5} \\
x &\equiv 2 \pmod{7} \\
x &\equiv 3 \pmod{9} \\
x &\equiv 4 \pmod{11}
\end{align*}
$$

We need to find the **smallest positive integer** $ x $ that satisfies all these congruences.

---

### Step 1: Observe a Pattern

Looking at the congruences:

$$
\begin{align*}
x &\equiv 1 \pmod{5} \\
x &\equiv 2 \pmod{7} \\
x &\equiv 3 \pmod{9} \\
x &\equiv 4 \pmod{11}
\end{align*}
$$

We notice that in each case, the remainder is **one less than the modulus**:

$$
x \equiv -1 \pmod{5}, \quad x \equiv -1 \pmod{7}, \quad x \equiv -1 \pmod{9}, \quad x \equiv -1 \pmod{11}
$$

verified_state: The system of congruences is x ≡ 1 mod 5, x ≡ 2 mod 7, x ≡ 3 mod 9, x ≡ 4 mod 11.
The goal is to find the smallest positive integer x satisfying all four congruences.
